name: Warbler Woodworks
old_description: Curved Walnut Pedestal Side Table - Available now! Click for info.
about:
Warbler Woodworks operates from a shop in Waynesboro, Virginia, where a single craftsman designs and builds custom furniture using traditional joinery. The business began as a one-person workshop focused on handcrafted pieces for the local community and surrounding areas including Charlottesville, Harrisonburg, Richmond, and Washington, D.C.

The shop produces heirloom-quality furniture such as wine cabinets, office desks, settees, dining tables, side tables, and credenzas. Each piece is made one at a time using time-honored techniques including dovetail and mortise-and-tenon joinery, executed with a blend of hand tools and power tools. The maker selects local hardwoods — primarily black walnut and cherry, along with white oak, maple, hickory, and ash — for their grain, color, and strength.

Warbler Woodworks serves residential clients who commission custom pieces for their homes. The shop’s reach extends across the Shenandoah Valley and into the Mid-Atlantic region, with customers in Virginia’s major cities and the Washington, D.C. metro area.

The founder emphasizes that mass-produced furniture lacks the subtlety and durability of handcrafted work. By relying on traditional joinery rather than screws or bolts, and by finishing each piece to highlight the wood’s natural character, the shop aims to create furniture that tells a story and endures for generations.

name: Warfield Electric
old_description: Custom DC motor manufacturer serving OEM customers
about:
Warfield Electric was founded in 1974 in Upland, California. The company began as a specialist in DC motor repair and has since expanded into custom motor manufacturing and large-scale remanufacturing.

Today Warfield Electric operates as both a manufacturer and remanufacturer of AC and DC electric motors. Under the WEMOCO (Warfield Electric Motor Company) banner it builds custom DC motors for original equipment manufacturers, while its DC Connection division rejuvenates obsolete industrial motors and gearboxes. The company maintains six locations across the United States — Frankfort, Illinois; Upland, California; Conyers, Georgia; Waukesha, Wisconsin; Westland, Michigan; and Dallas, Texas — and stocks an inventory of over 10,000 motors available on an exchange basis. It produces new OEM DC motors for more than 15 global manufacturers and rebuilds drive units for brands such as Hyster, Yale, Crown, Toyota, and Raymond.

The company serves the wind energy sector with new pitch motors and remanufactured pitch and yaw motors for turbines from GE, AMD, SSB, Moog, Clipper, Adda, VEM, ABB, Lonne, AVN, and Bonfiglioli. In material handling it supplies remanufactured motors and drive units for forklifts and warehouse equipment. Additional markets include ground support equipment, agriculture, mining, airport facilities, cold storage, and brewery applications. Customers range from OEMs to independent repair shops such as Mahaffeys Electric Motor Repair and large fleet operators like Anderson Material Handling.

Warfield Electric emphasizes service, quality, and price as its founding principles. It promotes its remanufactured motors as engineered to or above OEM standards, highlights a knowledgeable on-site engineering staff, and stresses honest pricing to build long-term partnerships. The firm positions itself as the nation’s largest DC motor remanufacturer, leveraging a nationwide exchange program and the ability to produce custom motors in small quantities.

name: Wasatch Cable
old_description: Communication is the fabric upon which our company was founded.
about:
Wasatch Cable & Design, LLC operates from Springville, Utah, with a design and support presence in nearby Orem. The company was founded on the principle that communication is the fabric of its business, though a specific founding year is not publicly disclosed. Ownership details beyond the LLC structure are not stated, and founder names are not provided in available materials.

The company provides end-to-end cable assembly services, from design optimization for manufacturability through production and testing. It runs domestic design, engineering, and support functions while leveraging Pacific-Rim manufacturing facilities for cost-effective turn-key production. Capabilities include custom molded assemblies with unique connectors and over-molded strain reliefs, mechanically assembled cables, wire harnesses, and smart cables incorporating PCBs or discrete components. Every assembly undergoes 100% testing and is warranted against defects, and the firm offers stocking and warehousing programs to secure on-time delivery.

Wasatch Cable serves OEMs across a broad range of sectors, including point-of-sale, automotive, military, transportation, networking, radar, medical, and industrial automation. Its design gallery references applications such as USB, OBD, coaxial/RF, armored cables, video display, and legacy serial interfaces (RS-232, RS-442, RS-449), as well as injection-molded cases and enclosures.

The company emphasizes responsive communication and rapid turnaround on quotations, first articles, and final delivery as its primary differentiators. It positions itself as a no-nonsense engineering and manufacturing partner that accelerates customers' time to market through domestic design expertise combined with offshore production efficiencies.

name: Wasatch Container
old_description: Wasatch Container is Utah’s premier provider of integrated case and foam packaging solutions.
about:
Wasatch Container operates from North Salt Lake, Utah, where it was founded in 1995 by Jerry Frisch, a University of Wisconsin‑Stout packaging engineering graduate. The company began as a modest brown‑box manufacturer and remains family‑owned, with Frisch joined by his children Ryan Frisch and Lauren Frisch in leadership roles.

Today the firm runs three specialized manufacturing facilities in the Salt Lake City area totaling more than 225,000 square feet and employs over 85 people. Its core output includes custom corrugated boxes, point‑of‑purchase displays, protective foam inserts, wood crates, and rugged transport cases. In‑house capabilities span structural and graphic design, prepress, 3D rendering, digital sample cutting, die‑cutting, foam converting, fabricating, finishing, assembly, and fulfillment services such as kitting, e‑commerce packing, and U.S./Canada shipping.

The customer base covers telecommunications, industrial, medical, and aerospace shipping applications, as well as e‑commerce and retail brands requiring UN‑certified packaging, stock boxes, or high‑value product protection. Clients range from companies needing single‑run prototypes to those managing ongoing supply programs.

Wasatch Container emphasizes a collaborative four‑step process — Design & Discovery, Transparent Pricing, Production & Precision, and Ongoing Support — and highlights its award‑winning design team, full in‑house converting, and integrated case‑and‑foam approach as key differentiators.

about:
Washington Workplace operates from Arlington, Virginia, serving the Washington, D.C., Maryland, and Virginia corridor as well as clients nationwide. The company functions as an office furniture dealership, supplying contract furnishings and delivering a suite of workplace design services.

Its core offering combines product sales with end-to-end project execution. Services include space planning and design, budgeting, project management, furniture installation, office maintenance, and storage solutions. The firm handles projects ranging from complete workplace redesigns to targeted furniture refreshes, coordinating logistics and installation through its own teams.

The client base spans commercial offices, government agencies, and organizations throughout the DMV region seeking to improve workplace functionality and employee well‑being. Engagements typically begin with a free consultation to assess spatial needs, followed by furniture specification, procurement, and installation management.

Washington Workplace frames its differentiation around a partnership model that prioritizes occupant well‑being over transactional sales. The company’s stated philosophy — “People | Products | Ideas…that make a difference” — reflects a focus on guiding clients through the entire design‑to‑installation process rather than simply supplying catalog items.

name: Watson Furniture
old_description: Our standard finishes are guaranteed to ship the very next business day
about:
Watson Furniture traces its roots to 1966 when South African-born cabinetmaker and metalworker Grahame Watson opened a small workshop on Bainbridge Island, Washington. The company relocated to a 34-acre manufacturing campus in nearby Poulsbo and has remained family-owned since 2010, when Clif and Kathy McKenzie assumed majority ownership after a 1989 partnership with Bill Haggerty and Daniel Warn. Today the business is led by Chairman Clif McKenzie, President CK McKenzie, and Board Member Kathy McKenzie.

The company designs and manufactures furniture for two primary segments: modern office environments (desks, tables, systems, and storage) and mission-critical consoles for 24/7 control rooms and emergency communications centers. Production processes include a PFAS-free, heat-cured electrostatically applied coating, polypropylene edge banding as a PVC-free standard, and thermally fused low-pressure laminate fabrication. The Poulsbo facility handles all fabrication, finishing, and assembly in-house.

Customers include corporate offices, government agencies, and public-safety organizations that require durable, purpose-built furniture for high-stakes, round-the-clock operations. The firm’s pivot to mission-critical work began in 1986 when a local emergency communications center commissioned custom consoles, establishing a specialization that now runs alongside its commercial office line.

The company positions itself as fiercely independent, rooted in its community, and focused on integrity over shortcuts.

name: Wear X Apparel
old_description: Use the form below to contact us for any special requests, inquiries, questions or concerns
about:
Wear X Apparel operates from Rapid City, South Dakota. The company was founded by Scott Lucero, who brings over 20 years of experience in the custom apparel industry. Lucero established the business as a one-stop shop for apparel design and manufacturing, drawing on a background that includes collaborations with major entertainment, music, and sports properties.

The shop offers a full suite of decoration and production services: cut-and-sew assembly, large-format sublimation, roll-to-roll printing, direct-to-film transfer, embroidery, and screen printing. It handles both commercial and low-volume runs, with equipment geared for high-volume output when needed. No facility size or headcount figures are disclosed.

Clients span television (Sons of Anarchy, Gas Monkey Garage, The Walking Dead), music (Taylor Swift, The Rolling Stones, Billie Eilish, among others), rodeo (J.J. Harrison), motorsports (NHRA), energy drinks (Monster Energy), and hospitality (Aria Hotels and Casinos in Las Vegas). The company serves brands, entertainers, and corporate customers seeking custom apparel.

Wear X Apparel emphasizes its commitment to quality and customer satisfaction, positioning itself as an experienced, reliable partner that can manage projects from design through delivery. The founder’s industry relationships and the breadth of in-house capabilities are cited as key differentiators.
